Rijal, Weiskittel and Kershaw (2012) DBH–height models for the Acadian Region

Source: R/hd_rijal2012.R
hd_rijal2012.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the regional height–diameter equations of Rijal, Weiskittel and Kershaw (2012) for 15 tree species of the North American Acadian Region (Maine, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island and southern Québec). Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm), a climate-derived site index, stand crown competition factor and the tree's basal area in larger trees.

Usage

hd_rijal2012(
  DBH,
  species,
  CSI,
  CCF,
  BAL,
  variant = c("gnls", "nlme"),
  keep_model_id = FALSE
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height, in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PICE.RUB"; compact "PICERUB" is accepted).

CSI

Numeric vector. Plot level. Climate-derived site index (m): "a climate-derived estimate of site index (CSI) ... based on a non-parametric regression model that relates observed site index to local climate variables (Weiskittel et al., 2011b)" (source "CSI", p. 381). Units and base age are not stated; metres are assumed (they reproduce the observed mean heights). Must be > 0.

CCF

Numeric vector. Plot level. Stand crown competition factor (Krajicek et al. 1961), computed in the source with the maximum crown width equations of Russell and Weiskittel (2011) (source "CCF", pp. 380–381). Minimum tree size not stated. Must be >= 0.

BAL

Numeric vector. Tree level. Basal area of trees larger than the subject tree (source "BAL", p. 381). Units are not stated; m²/ha is assumed. Species basis and minimum DBH are not stated. Must be >= 0.

variant

Coefficient set: "gnls" (default; Table 5) or "nlme" (Table 6 fixed effects, random effects = 0).

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("rijal2012_gnls" or "rijal2012_nlme").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope (species coverage): American beech (FAGU.GRA), grey birch (BETU.POP), paper birch (BETU.PAP), trembling aspen (POPU.TRE), red maple (ACER.RUB), northern red oak (QUER.RUB), sugar maple (ACER.SAH), yellow birch (BETU.ALL), balsam fir (ABIE.BAL), black spruce (PICE.MAR), eastern hemlock (TSUG.CAN), red spruce (PICE.RUB), eastern white cedar (THUJ.OCC), eastern white pine (PINU.STR) and white spruce (PICE.GLA). Fitted to permanent and research plots, mostly in mixed-species, uneven-aged stands (pp. 380–381).

Model form (eq. 4, p. 381): $$HT = 1.37 + (c_0 + CSI^{c_3}) [1 - \exp(-c_1 DBH)]^{c_2 + c_4 \ln(CCF + 1) + c_5 BAL}.$$

Variants (chosen with variant): "gnls" (default) uses the generalized nonlinear least-squares coefficients (Table 5, p. 387), which the authors recommend "when no observations are available for local calibration" (p. 386). "nlme" uses the fixed effects of the nonlinear mixed-effects fit (Table 6, p. 387) with the source, stand and year random effects on \(c_0\) set to zero; without local calibration these were more biased than GNLS (p. 386). For grey birch and northern red oak the NLME BAL coefficient was not significant (printed "–") and is zero.

Height convention: total tree height. The 1.37 m intercept (US breast height) is used for all data, although Canadian DBH was measured at 1.3 m; the authors judged the difference negligible (p. 381). Predicted height is 1.37 m at DBH 0.

Rows with NA in any input return NA height. DBH outside the per-species range of the fitting data (Table 1, p. 381) is computed and reported in a single warning. The source gives no ranges for CSI, CCF or BAL; inputs extreme enough to make the exponent non-positive raise an error.

References

Rijal, B., Weiskittel, A.R., and Kershaw, J.A., Jr. (2012). Development of regional height to diameter equations for 15 tree species in the North American Acadian Region. Forestry, 85(3), 379–389. doi:10.1093/forestry/cps036

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

hd_rijal2012(
  DBH = c(10, 25, 40),
  species = c("PICE.RUB", "ABIE.BAL", "ACER.RUB"),
  CSI = 15, CCF = 150, BAL = c(20, 8, 2)
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   8.08
#> 2  16.1 
#> 3  18.8 

# Mixed-model fixed effects
hd_rijal2012(25, "PICE.RUB", CSI = 15, CCF = 150, BAL = 10,
             variant = "nlme", keep_model_id = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   height model_id      
#>    <dbl> <chr>         
#> 1   15.5 rijal2012_nlme

# Inside dplyr::mutate() with tree and plot data
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(12, 25, 18),
  species = c("PICE.RUB", "TSUG.CAN", "BETU.ALL"),
  CSI = c(14, 14, 17), CCF = c(180, 180, 120), BAL = c(18, 6, 12)
)
dplyr::mutate(trees, hd_rijal2012(DBH, species, CSI, CCF, BAL))
#>   DBH  species CSI CCF BAL    height
#> 1  12 PICE.RUB  14 180  18  9.243432
#> 2  25 TSUG.CAN  14 180   6 14.164134
#> 3  18 BETU.ALL  17 120  12 12.442150
